A QSP model of covalent KRAS G12C inhibition in NSCLC

Target engagement, adaptive MAPK feedback, resistance, and comparative efficacy

2026-11-04

1 Summary

This report documents a quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) model of covalent KRAS G12C inhibition in previously treated KRAS G12C–mutant non–small-cell lung cancer. The model couples oral pharmacokinetics, covalent engagement of a cycling (GDP/GTP) target, a lumped MAPK pathway with adaptive ERK→upstream negative feedback, and a two-clone tumour (KRAS-dependent sensitive + drug-tolerant resistant). It is calibrated to the published response and progression-free-survival endpoints of sotorasib, adagrasib and docetaxel, then validated out-of-sample and used for in silico trials and dose/schedule/combination exploration.

## 
## ```
##  Structural / a-priori identifiability notes:
## - Covalent potency (kcov_*) and free-exposure scale are only jointly identified; the exposure
##   scale (Cref) is fixed from PK so kcov_* carries the engagement efficiency.
## - Effect-site partition is not identifiable from these endpoints; effect-site = free plasma (fixed).
## - kprol and kdeath0 trade off in the net growth rate; only the net rate is informed, so both are
##   fixed from natural-history doubling time and only drug/resistance parameters are estimated.
## - A full differential-algebra structural analysis is out of scope; practical identifiability is
##   assessed here by the Hessian covariance, prior->posterior shrinkage and the objective profiles. 
## ```

11 Limitations

Effect-site is free plasma; the MAPK cascade is lumped to one ppERK output; resistance is two compartments plus a pre-existing fraction, not an explicit mutational spectrum; calibration uses summary-level published endpoints, not individual patient data. This is a research / educational in silico model and is not a clinical decision tool.
